explanations.8: The $host and $request_uri are built-in nginx variables that automatically capture the domain name and the full path/query string, so the redirect preserves exactly where the user was trying to go.
explanations.13: http2 is a faster protocol version; ssl means HTTPS encryption is enabled on port 443 (the standard secure port).
explanations.30: This tells nginx to use the server's preferred list of encryption methods instead of letting the client choose, which is more secure.
explanations.31: HIGH picks strong encryption methods, and the !aNULL:!MD5 parts exclude weak or broken ones that hackers could exploit.
explanations.34: The 'always' keyword ensures this custom header is added to every response, even error pages.
explanations.44: This rule tries to serve the requested file; if it doesn't exist, it falls back to index.html so client-side routing works for single-page apps like Docusaurus.
explanations.48: The ~* means case-insensitive pattern matching; this rule catches all static file types (images, fonts, stylesheets, etc.) by their file extension.
